## Summary

### The brain flags unexpected facial features within 140 ms

In this study, led by Cristiano Costa, we showed that EEG activity tracked precision-weighted prediction errors about facial features, peaking around 140 ms after the face appeared: predictions about what a face will do are checked and updated early in visual processing.

Costa C, Ward EK, Pezzetta R, Masina F, Arcara G, Press C, Scarpazza C (2026). Early electrophysiological responses reflect precision-weighted prediction errors to face features. *PLOS ONE*, 21(9), e0357956. DOI: [10.1371/journal.pone.0357956](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0357956)
